title: decisions.json - input of curation adjudicate-apply (schema 1.0)
description: The Daemon exports this task's decisions that are not applied yet (D32: decisions never cross tasks). Lines and decisions follow v1 (design doc 06, section 5.1): label = annotation conflict from skill_profile, task_verdict = task_success abstention, reject_appeal = appeal of a reject attributed to an appealable module; eef_check (C1 1.9) = an episode the EEF module could not settle, 'consistent' keeps it and 'inconsistent' rejects it as the gate's result; integrity_check (C1 1.11, design doc 14) = an episode the data integrity module suspects, 'intact' keeps it and 'broken' rejects it, likewise. 'discard' (drop the whole episode) wins over any task verdict; 'unsure' is recorded and changes nothing. adopt_suggestion always carries new_label here: the Daemon fills in the question's suggestion when a person left it out (C4 1.5.1). A task_verdict on an episode whose task_success did not abstain is a follow-up of its label answer (C1 follow_ups): adjudicate-apply counts it only while the label's latest decision is one of the follow-up's 'after' and the verdict came after it (by id), the same rule as the Daemon's queue; otherwise it lapses and the relabel is judged again.

relabel_rerun.description: how relabelled episodes without a human task verdict are judged again (D39): v1 = what v1's rejudge runs (multi-view scoring and the per-camera end-state vote only); full = the first run's complete task_success flow. Recorded with each relabel it applies, so a later retry of those episodes judges them the same way

line.description: a registry review line (C1, D43); adjudicate-apply refuses a line it has no apply rule for

decision.description: one of the line's decisions in the registry; the known lines are pinned below
